<thought>
I'm reviewing the PM's REST API design as a software architect, checking for architectural soundness, security gaps (auth/authz, rate limiting, multi-tenancy), consistency issues (the "404 Not Found change" typo, the succeeded/cancelling race), and scalability of the SSE/polling hybrid, then producing a refined architectural spec addressing these.

{"subject": "Flow Step Output", "description": "Architectural review and refinement of the Exaix request/plan REST interface", "steps": [{"step": 1, "title": "Architecture review findings", "description": "The PM draft is a solid functional skeleton but has gaps that matter at the architecture layer: (1) No authentication/authorization model specified — every endpoint must be scoped to an authenticated tenant/principal (A01/A07); without this, `GET /v1/requests/{id}` is an IDOR waiting to happen. (2) The `cancelling`→`succeeded` race in the transition table is correct behavior but underspecified as an architectural concern: it implies at-least-once delivery semantics between the executor and the status store, and the state write must be a single atomic compare-and-swap (\"complete wins over cancel\") to avoid a lost-update race under concurrent writers. (3) `GET /v1/requests/{id}` response line has a literal typo (\"304 Not Found change\") that must read `304 Not Modified`. (4) No rate-limit or payload-size bound stated on `POST /v1/requests`, which is the system's primary DoS surface. (5) SSE is specified without reconnection semantics — a dropped connection mid-stream needs a resume mechanism (`Last-Event-ID`) or clients will double-render or miss events. (6) No idempotency behavior defined for `POST /requests/{id}/cancel` itself (calling cancel twice on a `cancelling` request should be a no-op 202, not an error)."}, {"step": 2, "title": "Security & multi-tenancy additions", "description": "Every endpoint requires a Bearer token (short-lived signed JWT) or API key; `401` for missing/invalid credentials, `403` for valid-but-unauthorized principal — checked **after** resource resolution so a request belonging to another tenant returns `404`, not `403` (avoids resource-existence leakage across tenants, per A01). All queries (`GET /requests/{id}`, `GET /requests`, `POST /requests/{id}/cancel`, `GET /requests/{id}/plan`, `GET /requests/{id}/events`) are scoped by `tenant_id` derived from the authenticated principal, never from a request parameter. `POST /v1/requests` enforces a body size cap (e.g. 256KB) and is rate-limited per principal (`429` + `Retry-After`, per the existing error contract); `input` is validated against a JSON Schema before a Request row is created — reject unknown top-level fields rather than forwarding them into the Plan compiler (A03 template/expression-injection surface, since `input` eventually feeds a planner that may interpolate it into prompts or tool calls). All responses get standard security headers (HSTS, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'` since this is a pure JSON/SSE API with no HTML surface)."}, {"step": 3, "title": "Corrected status model — concurrency-safe", "description": "Same seven states and transition table as the PM draft, with one correction: the `304 Not Found change` typo in the GET response spec is `304 Not Modified`. Architecturally, the `running`→`cancelling`→{`cancelled`|`succeeded`} branch must be implemented as a single atomic conditional write at the status-store layer (e.g. `UPDATE requests SET status='cancelled' WHERE id=$1 AND status='cancelling'` racing against `UPDATE requests SET status='succeeded' WHERE id=$1 AND status IN ('running','cancelling')`) — whichever write lands first wins, and the loser's write is silently dropped (0 rows affected), not retried. This is a single source of truth invariant: exactly one terminal-state writer succeeds per Request. `POST /requests/{id}/cancel` becomes idempotent under this model: calling it while already `cancelling` returns `202` again (no-op), calling it on a terminal state returns `409` as specified."}, {"step": 4, "title": "SSE reliability and endpoint finalization", "description": "`GET /v1/requests/{id}/events` emits `id: <monotonic_seq>` on every SSE event; clients reconnecting send `Last-Event-ID`, and the server replays any buffered events with `seq > Last-Event-ID` from a short-lived (e.g. 5 min) ring buffer keyed by request ID before resuming live — if the buffer has already rolled past the requested sequence, the server sends a `event: resync` with the full current state (equivalent to a `GET /requests/{id}` snapshot) so the client can safely reset instead of silently missing events. The stream closes with a final terminal-state event and standard SSE stream end (no further reconnect needed once a terminal `event: status` with `succeeded`/`failed`/`cancelled` is observed). All six endpoints stand as designed by the PM (`POST /v1/requests`, `GET /v1/requests/{id}`, `GET /v1/requests`, `POST /v1/requests/{id}/cancel`, `GET /v1/requests/{id}/plan`, `GET /v1/requests/{id}/events`), now with: auth required on all six, tenant-scoping on all six, the `304 Not Modified` fix, cancel-idempotency, and SSE resume via `Last-Event-ID`."}]}
